Para a FAA, spray e gotas em geral não p: According to the FAA, sprays and drops usually do not protect enough, and oral decongestants can significantly impair performance.
Para a ICAO, o tímpano pode romper com 2: According to ICAO, the eardrum can rupture with a 200 to 500 mmHg difference; descending from 6,500 ft to sea level already gives about 150 mmHg.
Para o **passageiro**, a regra é a mesma: For **passengers**, the rule is the same as for the ear: with a sinus infection or severe congestion, they can **postpone** the flight and use a decongestant for relief. For **crew**, ANAC requires a **clear nose** and **no serious sinus disease**, with a sinus **X-ray** at the initial exam; ICAO requires no nasal obstruction. A cold is reassessed in **7 to 10 days**, and nobody flies with one.
Para o **passageiro**, o barotrauma em g: For **passengers**, barotrauma is usually not serious. Those with an **ear, nose or sinus infection** or **severe congestion** may **postpone the flight** to avoid pain and injury. For **crew**, the signs and symptoms of barotrauma **are not compatible with flying**: they return only after the acute process has fully passed and the eardrum examination is normal. A cold should be reassessed in **7 to 10 days**.
Para o **tripulante**, a ANAC e a ICAO u: For **crew**, ANAC and ICAO use **pure-tone audiometry**: up to **35 dB** at 500, 1,000 and 2,000 Hz and up to **50 dB** at 3,000 Hz, **in each ear**. At ANAC, the test is done every **5 years** under 40 and every **2 years** from 40. The FAA accepts hearing a **conversational voice at 1.8 m**, back turned, or a better-ear and worse-ear table. Anyone above the limit may still be fit if they **understand speech in cockpit noise**, in a special test or in flight. At ANAC, anyone failing in both ears is restricted from **using the radio** and from working as **cabin crew**.
Para o **tripulante**, a ANAC exige dent: For **crew**, ANAC requires enough teeth to chew without symptoms, **no deep decay**, gum or root disease, **no dental dressing** and **no root canal treatment in progress**, with a dental chart every **5 years** and a panoramic X-ray at the initial exam. Flying with barodontalgia means flying with pain that can **distract** or **incapacitate** on descent.
Para o **tripulante**: a ICAO e a ANAC e: For **crew**: ICAO and ANAC require no **vestibular disorder**, no **significant tube dysfunction** and no **unhealed perforation**; a **single dry perforation** does not make unfit, provided hearing meets the requirement. At ANAC, a **permanent** vestibular disorder makes unfit, and a **transient** one does until the condition recovers. After **stapedectomy**, ICAO asks for **1 to 3 months without flying**, specialist assessment and then flying restricted to **multi-crew for 2 years**. **Tympanoplasty** with an intact eardrum and normal hearing leaves no restriction. At the FAA, a **resolved** perforation without symptoms allows issuing the certificate, and ear surgery is decided by the FAA itself with the surgeon's report; **transient** vertigo, such as acute labyrinthitis or benign positional vertigo, may not disqualify after full recovery.
Para voar, é preciso **entender a fala e: To fly, you need to **understand speech and the radio** in cockpit noise, hear **warning signals** and the sounds of the aircraft itself. Speech is concentrated between **500 and 3,000 Hz**, and that is the range in which authorities measure hearing. Loss can be **conductive**, in the outer and middle ear, or **sensorineural**, in the inner ear and nerve; **presbycusis**, age-related loss, can begin after **30** and affects high-pitched sounds first.

Voar com sinusite é arriscar uma dor que: Flying with sinusitis risks pain that can **incapacitate** the pilot on approach. Secretion trapped in the blocked sinus favors **infection**. The pain usually eases within minutes with a **mild nasal vasoconstrictor**, but anyone on **antibiotics** or **antihistamines** does not fly during treatment.
Voar com uma vertigem ativa ou cedo dema: Flying with active vertigo or too soon after surgery risks **incapacitation** mid-descent. Anyone who had stapes surgery must know that **colds** and nasal infections threaten middle ear ventilation.
Voar ouvindo mal é arriscar **perder uma: Flying with poor hearing risks **missing an instruction** from control or an **alarm**. Voar resfriado é o caminho mais comum pa: Flying with a cold is the most common route to barotrauma. **Se um laser atingir a cabine:** não ol: **If a laser hits the cockpit:** do not look at the beam, **shield your eyes** with your hand or the sun visor and, if there are two pilots, the one who was not hit takes the controls. After landing, report it: in Brazil, on CENIPA's **notification form**; in the US, on the FAA questionnaire.

A **acuidade visual** mede o menor detal: **Visual acuity** measures the smallest detail the eye can resolve. The unit is **1 minute of arc**, the gap the normal eye can distinguish; someone who sees that detail at 6 m has **6/6** acuity, the same as **20/20** in feet or **1.0** in decimal. The letter chart was created by **Snellen** in 1862. Many people with normal eyes see better than that, between **6/5 and 6/3**.
A **adaptação ao escuro** leva **até 30: **Dark adaptation** takes **up to 30 minutes**: the cones adjust in a few minutes and the rods keep gaining sensitivity afterwards. A strong light for **1 second or more** undoes part of that gain; the shorter flashes of anti-collision lights do not. Closing one eye in front of a strong light preserves that eye's adaptation.
A **cirurgia refrativa** tira o grau esc: **Refractive surgery** removes the prescription by sculpting the cornea with a laser. In **PRK**, the laser works on the surface; in **LASIK**, the surgeon lifts a thin **flap**, applies the laser and puts it back; the FAA treats **SMILE** the same way. ICAO notes that there is rarely any reason to have surgery **just to pass the exam**. The risks that matter in flight are **glare**, **halos**, loss of **contrast**, vision that varies during the day and **return of the prescription**; the LASIK flap can **dislodge** months later, sometimes from **rubbing the eye**.
A **lente de contato** é aceita se for *: A **contact lens** is accepted if it is **monofocal**, **untinted** and **well tolerated**, always with spare glasses. A contact lens and glasses are not used **on the same eye**, nor is **monovision**, one eye corrected for distance and the other for near, because the near eye sees poorly at a distance. People with very high prescriptions use contact lenses or **high-index** glasses, which distort the edges less.
A **luz vermelha** na cabine não atrapal: **Red light** in the cockpit does not hinder adaptation, but it **distorts the colors** of charts and worsens reading for people with presbyopia. In commercial aviation, almost everything comes from the instruments, and ICAO considers that the small gain from red light or dim white light does not make up for the loss in reading. In general aviation, dark adaptation still matters in many situations.
A **presbiopia**, a vista cansada, chega: **Presbyopia**, age-related farsightedness, comes slowly: first reading fails **in low light** or when tired, and the **hyperope** feels it earlier. The pilot must have a **single pair** that works for distance and near, without changing or removing the glasses: **half-eye**, **bifocal**, **trifocal** or **multifocal**. Full-lens reading glasses **are not acceptable**, because they blur the runway. When presbyopia appears, the right thing is to get the glasses right away, without waiting for small print to fail in daylight.
A **velocidade** também cobra: um movime: **Speed** also takes its toll: motion above **10° per second** in the visual field already blurs the image. Instrument **vibration** between **22 and 64 Hz**, common in helicopters, and the **2 to 10 Hz** vibration of turbulence hinder reading (See M1V6 - IV). In aerobatics and military flying, **G force** darkens vision before it knocks out consciousness (See M1V7 - II).
A **visão de um olho só** tem campo meno: **One-eyed vision** has a smaller field and loses **stereopsis**, 3D vision up close, but does not lose depth perception at a distance: beyond about **10 m**, it comes from shadows, apparent size, perspective and the shift of objects as the head moves. ANAC only accepts a **monocular** crew member at revalidation or at the exam after an accident or serious incident, if the good eye meets the requirements; ICAO, only as an exception, after **at least 6 months** of adaptation and a flight test. Flight **visual illusions** are covered in M2V5.
A ANAC pede 20/30 em cada olho e 20/20 b: ANAC requires 20/30 in each eye and 20/20 binocular for 1st class, with or without correction.

A aviação fala em cores: **vermelho**, *: Aviation speaks in colors: **red**, **green**, **yellow**, **amber**, **blue**, **cyan**, **magenta** and **white** appear on displays, aircraft lights and runways. The greatest risk is confusing **red, white and green** signals, and it gets worse in **low light** and with faint colors. In 2002, on a night landing in **Tallahassee**, the first officer's color deficiency on **FedEx 1448** hindered reading the red and white lights of the **PAPI**, the approach slope indicator.
A cabeça se move para olhar atrás das co: The head moves to look behind the windshield posts.
The cabin changes vision in several ways. Even when pressurized, **mild hypoxia** can impair **dark adaptation**, narrow the **visual field**, lower **acuity** and slightly raise the **pressure inside the eye** (See M2V1 - IV). The field can shrink as low as **1,000 to 1,500 m** (about **3,300 to 4,900 ft**); at night, without oxygen, vision can worsen above **5,000 ft**, and smokers feel it sooner.
A cirurgia de **retina** às vezes termin: **Retinal** surgery sometimes ends with a **gas bubble** inside the eye. With the lower cabin pressure, the gas **expands**, eye pressure rises and the person can **lose vision** severely. That is why **no one flies** until the gas is absorbed: about **2 weeks** with **SF6** and **6 weeks** with **C3F8** or **C2F6**. Other surgery inside the eye or a **penetrating injury** to the eye require at least **7 days**. For crew, retinal detachment means unfit until evaluation; the British authority asks for the surgeon's report at a **3-month** review.

A pilocarpina contrai a pupila e borra o: Pilocarpine constricts the pupil and blurs focus; the FAA does not accept it, and ICAO generally does not allow miotics.
A retina tem **três tipos de cone**, mai: The retina has **three types of cone**, most sensitive to **red**, **green** and **blue**; mixing the three gives every color. When one of them is missing or works less, **dyschromatopsia** appears, loosely called color blindness. About **8% of men** and **0.8% of women** fail the strictest tests, and **more than 99%** of them have a **red-green** deficiency. The congenital deficiency passes through the X chromosome and **does not worsen** over time.
A visão fica cinza e depois preta: Vision turns gray and then black
A visão noturna é das primeiras funções: Night vision is among the first functions to suffer from **hypoxia** (See M2V1 - IV). Without oxygen, it worsens above **5,000 ft** at night, and **smokers**, with carbon monoxide in the blood, feel it at even lower altitude. In the dark, the **pupil dilates**, the image loses sharpness and the eye tends to focus near, **night myopia**, of up to several diopters.
A área vista pelos dois olhos dá a visão: The area seen by both eyes gives 3D vision up close and removes the "hole" the nose makes in each eye's field.

Na **catarata**, troca-se a lente opaca: In **cataract** surgery, the opaque lens is replaced with an **intraocular lens**. Many people see well the very next day, and the prescription stabilizes in **6 to 8 weeks**. Passengers can fly **24 hours** later. For crew, ICAO considers only the **monofocal** lens suitable; the FAA also accepts lenses for presbyopia, if there is no glare or halos, and applies the same 3-month rule. The British authority keeps the pilot off for **at least 6 weeks**. Months or years later, the capsule may cloud over; the **YAG laser** fixes it in minutes.

No voo, **ver é o primeiro passo** de qu: In flight, **seeing is the first step** of almost every reaction: the pilot perceives, decides and only then acts. The eye has two types of light-sensing cell. **Cones** sit in the center, in the **fovea**, and provide **color** and **detail** in bright light; **rods** sit around them and work in **low light**, without color. Only the fovea sees sharply: just **10°** away from it, acuity already falls to **6/30**, five times worse than normal.

O **ar seco** da cabine resseca e irrita: The cabin's **dry air** dries and irritates the eyes on long flights, and **soft contact lenses** start to bother sooner. The eye does not have trapped air like the ear, with one serious exception: the **gas** the surgeon injects into the eye after retinal surgery **expands** with altitude (See M1V1 - II and M2V4 - VIII).
O **glaucoma** lesa o nervo óptico, em g: **Glaucoma** damages the optic nerve, usually with high **eye pressure**, and starts by taking away pieces of the **visual field** without symptoms. ICAO says to refer anyone with pressure of **24 mmHg** or more, or a difference of **5 mmHg** between the eyes. Under the FAA, the examiner can clear someone with pressure up to **23 mmHg** in both eyes, a **normal visual field** and accepted eye drops; normal-tension glaucoma, secondary glaucoma and filtering surgery go to the FAA for decision.
O **olho seco** piora no ar seco da cabi: **Dry eye** worsens in the cabin's dry air; **preservative-free** artificial tears help, and those with preservatives irritate contact lens wearers. **Conjunctivitis** and **corneal injury** need treatment before flying. A contact lens is a **foreign body**: it can scratch the cornea and cause allergy, ulcers and infection, which is why it needs follow-up.
O **passageiro** pode voar **24 horas**: **Passengers** can fly **24 hours** after corneal laser surgery, if the surgeon clears them. **Crew** wait longer. **ANAC** requires more than **6 months** since surgery and, if requested, normal **glare** and **contrast sensitivity** tests. **ICAO** suggests counting from when the eye drops are stopped: **3 months** with a prescription of up to 6 diopters; between 6 and 10, **3 months** for LASIK and **6** for PRK; above 10, **6 months**. Under the **FAA**, after **3 months**, recovered, with no medication and no symptoms, the case is generally not a concern; before that, only with the eye doctor's report confirming recovery.

O defeito também pode ser **adquirido**,: The deficiency can also be **acquired**, in one eye more than the other and sometimes worsening: diseases of the **retina**, the **optic nerve**, advanced **glaucoma** and medicines such as **hydroxychloroquine**, **ethambutol** and **digitalis**. **Sildenafil**, for erectile dysfunction, makes everything look **bluish** in **3% to 11%** of users for up to 5 hours or more; the FAA requires **8 hours** without flying after it (See M2V4 - VII).
O exame começa com as **placas pseudoiso: The exam starts with **pseudoisochromatic plates**, such as the **Ishihara** plates, viewed in daylight; anyone who fails may take other tests, such as the **D-15** color arrangement, lanterns and the **anomaloscope**. Lenses that "correct" color **do not count**. **ANAC** accepts anyone who reads the plates or, at least, recognizes the basic aviation colors in isolation: **yellow, blue, green, red, white, black and amber**. Under **ICAO**, anyone who fails and cannot distinguish navigation colors and lights is left with a Class 2 **valid by day** only. Under the **FAA**, since **2025** screening is done **once**, on a computer; anyone who fails receives a 3rd class **for day visual flight only**.

O gás se expande na cabine e pode causar: The gas expands in the cabin and can cause severe vision loss; the wait is about 2 weeks with SF6 and 6 weeks with C3F8.
O olho vê um **campo** largo, mas nítido: The eye sees a wide **field**, but sharp only in the center. With the gaze fixed, a normal eye reaches about **95°** to the outer side, **60°** toward the nose, **60°** upward and **75°** downward; one eye alone covers about **140°** horizontally. The periphery perceives **motion**, but not detail: to identify an aircraft, you have to bring it onto the **fovea**.
O passageiro pode voar com o colírio que: Passengers can fly with the eye drops their doctor prescribed, carrying them in their carry-on bag.
O problema é grande: nos EUA, os pilotos: The problem is large: in the US, pilots reported **12,840** cases in **2024** and **328 injuries** since 2010. In Brazil, endangering an aircraft or hindering air navigation is a **crime** (Penal Code, art. 261), with **2 to 5 years' imprisonment**. In the US, it is a federal crime, with up to 5 years in prison, and the FAA civil penalty reaches **US$11,000** per violation.

A **cinetose**, o enjoo de movimento, su: **Motion sickness** arises when the eyes, the inner ear and the body send messages that do not match: the inner ear feels the turbulence, the eyes see a still cabin. It comes with yawning, pallor, cold sweat, nausea and vomiting. Children under **2 years** rarely get sick; the peak is between **7 and 12 years**. Women are slightly more susceptible, and people with **migraine**, vertigo or inner-ear disease get sick more often.
A **desorientação espacial** é a ideia e: **Spatial disorientation** is the pilot's wrong idea of the aircraft's position, attitude and motion. It is common: many pilots have experienced it, and **5% to 10%** of general aviation accidents are attributed to it, with **90%** of those accidents **fatal**. In questionnaires with more than 3,000 airline pilots, vertigo and disorientation were **4%** of the in-flight incapacitations reported.
The **Coriolis illusion** is the strongest. In a long turn, an abrupt **head** movement, to pick up a chart from the floor or to look back, makes the body feel a rotation about another axis, almost impossible to ignore. That is why, in a turn and in cloud, the head stays **still**.
A **vertigem por cintilação** não vem do: **Flicker vertigo** does not come from the inner ear, but it confuses just the same: a light flashing **4 to 20 times per second**, such as the sun cut by the propeller or the anti-collision light reflecting in cloud, can cause nausea, dizziness and, in sensitive people, loss of consciousness. For passengers, these illusions pose no risk; for pilots, they are a known cause of accidents.
A **vertigem** verdadeira, a sensação de: True **vertigo**, the sensation of spinning, is something else: it comes from inner-ear disease, such as **Ménière's disease**, **vestibular neuritis** and **positional vertigo**, or from pressure, such as **alternobaric vertigo** on descent. For crew, ANAC and ICAO do not accept a permanent vestibular disorder; a transient one grounds until recovery. Waiting times and surgeries are in M2V3 (See M2V3 - III).

Feeling on the ground how the inner ear deceives, in a **Bárány chair** or a **disorientation simulator**, teaches you to recognize the conflict when it shows up in flight. A segunda é o **treino por instrumentos*: The second is **instrument training**. The FAA recommends training and maintaining proficiency in controlling the aircraft by instruments **before** flying with less than **3 miles** of visibility. At night and in poor visibility, the instruments are the reference, together with what is seen outside, and they must be tested before takeoff.
A terceira é **planejar**: conferir o te: The third is **planning**: check the weather before departure, en route and at the destination; know the region's geography; do not attempt visual flight when the weather may close in; keep night flying current. In the **somatogravic illusion**, the acceleration of a takeoff or go-around without visibility feels like **nose-up**; the pilot pushes the stick and may fly the aircraft into the ground. In children, any medication calls for caution, and scopolamine should be avoided.

Carry your medicines in your carry-on bag and keep to the **schedule**, especially with Parkinson's, adjusting to the time zone with your doctor. With multiple sclerosis, carry the neurologist's report listing the medicines you take. With dementia, travel with a **companion** who knows the routine. Take your medicines on schedule, including the anticoagulant (See M2V2 - VII), drink water and move your legs. Anticonvulsants are **incompatible** with crew duties: anyone who needs them does not fly as a pilot until the authority's waiting period is met.

Na crise **tônico-clônica**, o corpo enr: In a **tonic-clonic** seizure, the body stiffens for **15 to 20 seconds** and then shakes; it usually all ends within **1 to 2 minutes**, followed by confusion, drowsiness and body aches. In a **complex focal** seizure, the person is unaware for a minute or two, with repetitive movements. A **focal** seizure suggests a lesion in the brain that must be looked for. The **EEG** is normal in up to **40%** of people with epilepsy, so the **history** weighs more than the test.
Nas duas primeiras semanas depois do AVC: In the first two weeks after a stroke, the passenger flies with oxygen and an escort.
Nem toda pancada na cabeça machuca o **c: Not every blow to the head injures the **brain**. **Traumatic brain injury** means there was loss or alteration of consciousness, a neurological sign or a lesion on imaging. Severity is measured by **post-traumatic amnesia**, the time until memory works again without gaps: up to **1 hour** is mild, **1 to 24 hours** moderate, **1 to 7 days** severe and longer than that very severe.
No **Parkinson**, os sinais são tremor e: In **Parkinson's**, the signs are resting tremor, **stiffness** and **slowness** of movement, progressing slowly in some and quickly in others. In **multiple sclerosis**, the immune system attacks the myelin of the brain and spinal cord, usually between **20 and 40 years** of age, with relapses and remissions: tingling, weakness, changes in vision, speech or bladder. In **dementia**, the problem is memory and judgment; in **transient global amnesia**, the person loses recent memory for up to **24 hours** and then returns to normal.
No avião, síncope e pré-síncope são a **: On aircraft, syncope and presyncope are the **most common emergency**: **37.4%** of cases in a series of almost 12,000 in-flight emergencies. **Dehydration** from the dry air, **alcohol**, fasting, waiting on your feet in the lavatory queue and standing up quickly after hours of sitting all play a part. The cabin's **mild hypoxia** adds to the other factors (See M2V1).

No voo, a enxaqueca tem vários **gatilho: In flight, migraine has several **triggers** at once: the cabin's relative hypoxia, **short sleep**, **skipped meals**, time zones, **noise**, strong sun, stress and **alcohol**, red wine in particular. ICAO also lists cheese and chocolate. For passengers, known, rare or controlled migraine **is no problem**; the exception is a severe, frequent attack with vomiting and prostration.
No voo, o risco é a crise chegar com **p: In flight, the risk is a seizure arriving with **sleep deprivation**, interrupted sleep or **jet lag**, which lower the threshold. On board, the medical kit rarely has an anticonvulsant, and a long seizure may force a **diversion**. For passengers, the UK CAA asks to wait at least **24 hours** after a seizure; anyone with **uncontrolled** epilepsy or a **new** seizure needs medical clearance, and AsMA advises against flying after a seizure in the **last month**.

O **AVC** é a falta de sangue numa parte: A **stroke** is a lack of blood in part of the brain. In **85%** of cases it is **ischemic**, a blocked vessel; the rest are **hemorrhagic**, a ruptured vessel. A **transient ischemic attack** (TIA) gives the same signs but passes on its own: it is a warning, because about **30%** of people who have a TIA will have a stroke within 5 years. High blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, smoking, atrial fibrillation and carotid disease are the risk factors.
O **cérebro** não guarda reserva de oxig: The **brain** keeps no oxygen reserve: it depends on blood every second. That is why it is the first organ to feel the **cabin**. At **8,000 ft**, the saturation of someone at rest falls to around **93%** (See M2V2 - I); a healthy person does not even notice, but the lack of oxygen slows thinking long before it causes symptoms (See M2V1 - IV).

Voar deprimido ou em crise de ansiedade: Flying while depressed or in an anxiety crisis is flying with **subtle incapacitation**: slower, distracted, indecisive. For crew members, hiding the diagnosis or the medicine from the examiner breaks the rules and can invalidate the certificate. For passengers, **stable** depression and anxiety do not prevent flying; **fear of flying** can turn into hyperventilation on board and is treatable: cognitive-behavioural therapy works for many people.
Voar sob efeito é voar com o julgamento: Flying under the influence is flying with impaired judgement, and it is an **offence** under the rules. For passengers, using alcohol to sleep on the flight does not help sleep, and disruptive behaviour can prevent the flight. People with dependence should **detoxify before** travelling, so they do not go into withdrawal mid-flight. Sleeping pills count too: short-acting sedatives require **8 to 12 hours** before any aviation duty (See M2V8).

**Surto a bordo: como abordar.** Sintoma: **An episode on board: how to approach it.** Psychiatric symptoms account for up to **3%** of in-flight medical emergencies, and intoxication or withdrawal for as many again. The **crew** manages the situation and informs the captain; a health professional who volunteers states their training and does not act if they have been drinking or have taken a medicine that affects judgement. The first step is **conversation**: build rapport, try to calm the person and ask about the diagnosis, the medicines, the last dose and whether they are on board. Then look for another cause: **alcohol and drugs**, intoxication or withdrawal, vital signs and breathing, with water and oxygen if needed.

**Como prevenir e amenizar.** Antes de v: **How to prevent and ease it.** Before flying, agree with your doctor on the timing of your medicines in the destination time zone. In flight, drink water, walk down the aisle when the seat belt sign allows and eat at your usual times, carrying a snack in case of delay. Those who use insulin carry extra, split between two bags in the carry-on, and tell the crew.
**Como prevenir e amenizar.** Faça os ex: **How to prevent and ease it.** Have your follow-up tests done before long trips and do not skip the dose on the day of the flight. **Como prevenir e amenizar.** Meça o açú: **How to prevent and ease it.** Check your sugar before boarding and during the flight, every 4 to 6 hours or before meals; sensor users check the alarm. **Como prevenir e amenizar.** Prefira o: **How to prevent and ease it.** Choose an **aisle** seat and get up to walk when the seat belt sign allows; move your calves while seated. On flights of more than 6 hours, people at risk may wear **compression stockings** of 15 to 30 mmHg, with medical advice. Drink water. Those with apnoea or hypoventilation take the hypoxia test beforehand and arrange oxygen or CPAP with the airline. Crew: weight-loss medicine only with a prescription and with the waiting period completed.

At the destination, shift to local time gradually, as agreed with your doctor.
**Remédios e voo.** A **levotiroxina** é: **Medicines and flight.** **Levothyroxine** is taken on an empty stomach, once a day; on a trip across time zones, keep the interval at about 24 hours and adjust gradually to local time. Antithyroid drugs require follow-up blood tests. Beta blockers, used for a racing heart, follow the high blood pressure rules for crew (See M2V2 - II).
**Remédios e voo.** O que pesa é o risco: **Medicines and flight.** What matters is the risk of hypoglycaemia and the time to adapt to the medicine. Metformin, gliptins, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 drugs lower sugar little when used alone; SGLT2 inhibitors make you urinate more and can dehydrate you in the dry cabin. Sulfonylureas, glinides and insulin require checking sugar and observing the waiting periods. Never change the dose on your own before a trip.
**Remédios e voo.** Os remédios do tipo: **Medicines and flight.** **GLP-1** medicines often cause nausea and take away appetite; alone, they lower sugar little, but eating and drinking little on the flight can dehydrate you and cause dizziness. Combined with diabetes medicines, the risk of low sugar rises. Stimulant weight-loss medicines speed up the heart and disrupt sleep.

The **insulin pump** feels the pressure. On the climb, cabin pressure falls, bubbles grow in the reservoir and the pump delivers extra insulin, about **1 to 1.4 units**; on the descent, it draws back and delivers almost 1 unit less. The authors suggest disconnecting the pump before take-off, removing the bubbles and reconnecting at **cruise**; after landing, disconnecting again and priming the tubing with **2 units**. Agree with your doctor before changing how you use it.
A **insulina** vai na **bagagem de mão**: **Insulin** goes in your **carry-on**, never only in checked luggage: the hold can get cold enough to **freeze** insulin, and the bag can get lost. Carry **extra** insulin, split between **two bags**, ideally one with a travel companion, in a **cool bag**. During the flight, it does not need a fridge. Carry your doctor's letter and an ID stating that you use insulin.
The **thyroid** is the body's accelerator. In **hypothyroidism**, it works slowly: tiredness, sleepiness, feeling cold, weight gain, slow thinking. In **hyperthyroidism**, it speeds up: racing heart, tremor, anxiety, feeling hot and weight loss, sometimes with arrhythmia (See M2V2 - IV). In **Graves' disease**, the eyes may bulge and **double vision** may appear (See M2V4 - VII).

A hipoglicemia vem quase sempre do **tra: Hypoglycaemia almost always comes from **treatment**: insulin, **sulfonylureas** and **glinides** are the medicines that lower sugar the most; **metformin** alone, well controlled, rarely causes it. Flying brings the triggers together: a delayed meal, time zones, effort on the ground, alcohol on the layover. The FAA considers it symptomatic hypoglycaemia when sugar is **70 mg/dL** or less.

No **diabetes**, o açúcar do sangue fica: In **diabetes**, blood sugar is high because insulin is lacking (**type 1**) or because the body responds poorly to it (**type 2**). For flying, the greatest danger is not high sugar but **low sugar**, **hypoglycaemia**: tremor, sweating, hunger, confusion and, if nothing is done, fainting and even coma. It is a **sudden incapacitation**. Very high sugar also gets in the way: blurred vision, tiredness and slow thinking.
No **hipertireoidismo**, o remédio antit: In **hyperthyroidism**, an antithyroid drug without side effects does not disqualify, but the pilot is unfit until function returns to normal, and for 1st class the ophthalmologist checks **eye movements** and double vision. After **surgery** or **radioactive iodine**, grounding lasts until the end of treatment and stable function, with a blood test every year. ANAC assesses significant over- or underfunction and the effects of replacement hormone case by case.

In flight, obesity weighs on three points. **Breathing**: in **obesity hypoventilation syndrome**, about **90%** have apnoea, and even those with normal oxygen during the day may have **low oxygen** in the cabin; that is why a **hypoxia test** is recommended before flying (See M2V1 - VII). **Circulation**: a BMI of 30 or more is a risk factor for **thrombosis**, and sitting by the window, in this group, multiplied the risk by about **6** in one study (See M2V2 - VII). And **sleep**: more than **90%** of people with a BMI of 40 or more have apnoea that needs treatment (See M2V8 - VII).

No voo, o hipotireoidismo sem tratamento: In flight, untreated hypothyroidism makes the crew member slower and more tired, with less attention over long hours. Hyperthyroidism makes the heart work close to its limit, with less margin for lack of oxygen and for stress; and double vision hampers reading the instruments and the approach. Treated and stable, the thyroid almost never prevents flying.

O **ar seco** (Veja M1V1 - IV) e a **imo: **Dry air** (See M1V1 - IV) and **immobility** add up the risks. High sugar makes you urinate more and dehydrates you. **Obesity**, with a BMI of **30** or more, is a risk factor for thrombosis on trips of more than **4 hours** (See M2V2 - VII). And the cramped cabin limits movement precisely for those who most need to walk.
O **fuso horário** mexe nos remédios (Ve: **Time zones** affect medicines (See M2V8 - III). Flying **east**, the day gets shorter; flying **west**, longer. When the day loses or gains more than **2 hours**, the insulin dose may need adjusting. Insulin travels in the **carry-on**: in the hold, the cold may freeze it, and the bag may get lost.
O **fuso** muda a conta. Indo para o **l: **Time zones** change the maths. Flying **east**, the day gets shorter: if it loses more than **2 hours**, the intermediate or long-acting insulin dose may need to be reduced. Flying **west**, the day gets longer: if it gains more than 2 hours, an extra dose of rapid-acting insulin with a meal may be needed. People on oral medicines rarely need an extra dose. Keeping your watch on departure time during the flight helps space out meals.
O **glicosímetro** funciona na cabine: a: The **glucose meter** works in the cabin: the pressure at 6,000 to 8,000 ft does not affect most devices, but extreme cold, heat or altitude can disturb the meter and the strips, another reason to carry them in the carry-on. The continuous sensor and the pump also travel with you; ask the airline in advance for a seat near the toilet if you want privacy to inject.
O **gás que expande** na subida (Veja M1: **Gas that expands** on the climb (See M1V1 - II) also reaches insulin. In the **insulin pump**, bubbles grow in the reservoir and push the liquid: in one study, the pumps delivered about **1 to 1.4 extra units** on the climb and almost 1 unit less on the descent. For those on small doses, such as children, the difference matters.
O **índice de massa corporal** (**IMC**): The **body mass index** (**BMI**) is weight in kilograms divided by height squared. From **18.5 to 24.9** is a healthy weight; from **25 to 29.9**, overweight; from **30** upward, **obesity**. The number does not tell everything, but it points to those more likely to have apnoea, high blood pressure, diabetes and thrombosis, problems that flying worsens.

O protocolo britânico funciona: **49 pil: The British protocol works: **49 pilots** flew **22,078 hours** over 7.5 years, with **97.7%** of readings in the green and **no incapacitation**. In the low red, below **4 mmol/L** (about 72 mg/dL), the pilot hands over control to the co-pilot, eats **10 to 15 g** of fast-acting carbohydrate and checks again in **15 minutes**. For crew, flying without declaring the diabetes or the medicine is a violation and may invalidate the certificate and insurance.

Os **hormônios** são mensageiros do sang: **Hormones** are messengers in the blood. **Insulin** takes sugar out of the blood and into the cells; the **thyroid** sets the speed of metabolism; fat also produces signals that affect appetite and blood pressure. Flying rarely alters these hormones directly: it changes the **routine** around them, such as mealtimes, medicine timing, sleep and movement.
Os **remédios para emagrecer** mudaram o: **Weight-loss medicines** have changed the picture. **Semaglutide**, **liraglutide** and **tirzepatide** are accepted: the FAA requires **1 week** without flying at the start and **48 hours** after each dose increase; the UK requires **2 weeks** at the start, with an examiner's assessment, and **72 hours** after each adjustment. **Orlistat** requires 48 hours with the FAA. **Phentermine**, alone or with topiramate, and the combination of **naltrexone with bupropion** are not accepted. Products bought without a prescription, online, disqualify in the UK.

Outras autoridades já certificam pilotos: Other authorities already certify pilots on insulin. In **2019**, the **FAA** opened 1st and 2nd class to those using a **continuous sensor**: **6 months** of data, sugar between 70 and 180 mg/dL for **70%** of the time or more and less than **1%** below 54 mg/dL. The **UK** certifies airline pilots on insulin provided they fly **with a co-pilot**: they check sugar before the flight, every hour and **30 minutes** before landing, on a green, amber and red traffic light.
Para o **passageiro**, a obesidade não i: For **passengers**, obesity does not prevent flying, but it calls for planning. Those who have difficulty moving can request **special assistance** from the airline at least **48 hours** in advance, or **72 hours** if they need a companion or a medical document. The **CPAP** goes in the carry-on, with the doctor's letter. Anyone having **bariatric surgery** abroad should plan the return with the specialist before travelling.
Para o **passageiro**, a tireoide estáve: For **passengers**, a stable thyroid does not prevent flying. One practical point: after **radioactive iodine** treatment, the body can set off airport **radiation alarms** for up to about **95 days**. Carry the proof of treatment. A racing heart, shortness of breath or fever with an uncontrolled thyroid call for a doctor before travelling.
Para o **passageiro**, o diabetes **não: For **passengers**, diabetes **does not prevent** flying. The risk is hypoglycaemia far from the ground: the treatment is the same, fast-acting sugar and check again. Tell the crew that you use insulin, carry ID and a snack, and do not rely on the in-flight meal, which may be delayed. Very high sugar, vomiting or signs of ketoacidosis call for a doctor before boarding.

Para o tripulante, a ANAC considera inap: For crew, ANAC considers unfit for 1st class anyone with a **BMI of 40 or more**. In the UK and Europe, with a BMI of **35 or more**, the pilot is fit only after a risk assessment, including the heart and **apnoea screening**. The FAA does not use a single cut-off: the examiner calculates the BMI and assesses the risk of apnoea, which also appears at lower weights.
Para o tripulante, a regra é **afastar a: For crew, the rule is to **ground on diagnosis** and return when function is **normal and stable**. In **hypothyroidism**, the FAA clears at the exam itself those who are stable, without symptoms, on **levothyroxine** or another accepted hormone and with **TSH below 10** in the past year. In the UK, changing the dose by up to **25 µg**, without symptoms, does not ground; with symptoms, the crew member stays on the ground until better.
Para o tripulante, o Brasil e a ICAO seg: For crew, Brazil and ICAO follow the old rule: anyone using **insulin** is **unfit**. Without insulin, ANAC accepts diabetes controlled with diet or medicine; with an **oral hypoglycaemic**, after **60 days** of observation with good control, and the revalidated certificate is valid for **6 months** at most. The FAA requires a no-fly period with each new medicine: **14 days** for metformin, **30 days** for most others and **60 days** for sulfonylureas and glinides, with glycated haemoglobin up to **9**.

Quem já teve trombose ou tem outros fato: Those who have had thrombosis or have other risk factors: without the calf pump the blood returns slowly, dehydration makes it more concentrated, and those with a damaged vein or more active clotting form clots more easily (See M2V2 - VII)
Quem usa anticoagulante ou remédio de pr: Those on anticoagulants or blood pressure medicine: a late dose lets the blood clot or the pressure rise; an early dose adds to the previous one and can cause bleeding or a drop in pressure (See M2V8)
Pilotos de caça e de acrobacia: a aceler: Fighter and aerobatic pilots: acceleration pulls blood towards the legs; the heart has to overcome this heavier column of blood, and beyond the limit flow to the head falls (See M1V7)
Quem tem a abertura dos seios bloqueada:: Those whose sinus openings are blocked: the expanding air has no way out, pressure inside the sinus rises and the wall hurts
Resfriados, alérgicos e quem dorme na de: People with colds, allergies and those who sleep during descent: the Eustachian tube only opens when swallowing or yawning; swollen lining keeps it shut, sleepers do not swallow, and the vacuum in the middle ear pulls the eardrum inward
Mais de 85% dos casos de barotrauma: a i: More than 85% of barotrauma cases: inflammation swells the lining of the tube and of the sinus openings, and the passage becomes too narrow for air to pass
Cárie, restauração recente, canal ou les: Caries, recent filling, root canal or root lesion: gas trapped in the tooth or an inflamed pulp senses the pressure change, and pressure on the nerve causes pain
Quem já tem perda auditiva: tem menos cé: Those who already have hearing loss: fewer hair cells are working; noise masks speech more, and each new injury takes from an already smaller reserve (See M1V6)
Voo noturno sem oxigênio, fumantes: a re: Night flight without oxygen, smokers: the retina, especially the rods used for night vision, uses a lot of oxygen and feels the drop first; in smokers, carbon monoxide occupies part of the haemoglobin and adds hypoxia to that of the cabin
Voos longos, quem usa lente gelatinosa:: Long flights, soft contact lens wearers: dry air evaporates tears faster; the lens absorbs water and covers the cornea, which receives less tear film and less oxygen
Quem operou a retina com gás: a bolha fi: Those who had retinal surgery with gas: the bubble is trapped inside the closed eye; as it grows, eye pressure rises and can shut off the retinal artery
Quem voa para o sol, sem óculos de sol:: Those flying into the sun without sunglasses: above the clouds light arrives both direct and reflected; without a filter, the pupil closes and the eye is slow to readapt to the shaded panel
Pouso, turbulência, helicóptero: o olho: Landing, turbulence, helicopters: the eye shakes inside the orbit, and the reflex that stabilises the image cannot keep up with fast vibration
Acrobacia e voo militar: a pressão dentr: Aerobatics and military flight: pressure inside the eye opposes blood pressure; with high G blood reaches the head weakly, and the retina loses flow before the brain
Piloto sem treino de instrumentos: o lab: Pilots without instrument training: the inner ear senses changes in motion, not a sustained position; without the habit of trusting instruments, the brain follows the wrong sensation
Voo manual sem olhar a atitude: os canai: Hand flying without checking attitude: the semicircular canals do not register rotational acceleration below threshold, and a slow bank goes unnoticed
Espera em órbita, curvas em nuvem: o líq: Holding patterns, turns in cloud: the fluid in the semicircular canals catches up with the turn, the cupula returns to centre, and the inner ear starts reporting no rotation
Decolagem e arremetida sem visibilidade:: Take-off and go-around without visibility: the otoliths sense gravity and acceleration together; forward acceleration tilts the force they perceive as if the nose were rising
Quem olha para baixo ou para trás em cur: Those who look down or back during a turn: moving the head in one plane while the body rotates in another stimulates several semicircular canals at once (Coriolis effect)
Voo noturno longo, tripulante resfriado:: Long night flights, crew with a cold: hypoxia and fatigue make the brain slow to check the inner ear against the eyes; alcohol changes the density of the cupula, and a cold unbalances pressure between the two ears
Quem tem enxaqueca, doença pulmonar ou c: Those with migraine, lung or heart disease: the brain uses a lot of oxygen and cannot store it; with a diseased lung or heart the blood arrives poorer, and lack of oxygen is a migraine trigger
Quem operou a cabeça ou teve trauma rece: Those who had head surgery or recent trauma: air that entered the skull is trapped in a rigid box; as it grows, it compresses the brain
Quem tem epilepsia ou enxaqueca: a priva: Those with epilepsy or migraine: sleep deprivation makes neurons more excitable and lowers the seizure threshold; changing medicine timing changes its blood level
Quem já desmaiou, idosos, quem usa reméd: Those who have fainted before, older people, those on blood pressure medicine: blood pools in the legs; the reflex that tightens vessels and speeds the heart is slower in older people and blunted by medicine, and dehydration reduces blood volume
Quem tem enxaqueca: o cérebro com enxaqu: Those with migraine: the migraine brain reacts more to change; fasting lowers sugar and strong sensory stimulation excites neurons, two known triggers
AVC recente, epilepsia não controlada: o: Recent stroke, uncontrolled epilepsy: the injured brain has less reserve for lack of oxygen and the seizure may recur; on board there is no way to treat in time
Quem já está cansado, ansioso ou sob rem: Those already tired, anxious or on medication: planning and deciding are among the first brain functions to fail with little oxygen; fatigue, anxiety and sedatives already reduce them, and hypoxia adds up
Quem tem depressão ou ansiedade: o sono: Those with depression or anxiety: sleep helps regulate mood; in these conditions sleep and the body clock are often already disturbed, and deprivation makes emotional control more fragile
Tripulante com problemas pessoais: o est: Crew with personal problems: prolonged stress keeps cortisol and adrenaline high, worsens sleep and uses up attention that would be left for the flight
Quem bebe ou usa sedativo para dormir: á: Those who drink or use sedatives to sleep: alcohol and sedatives depress the brain and fragment deep sleep; the effect lasts longer than it feels, and the next day attention and reflexes remain slow
Passageiro com medo de voar: o medo disp: Passengers afraid of flying: fear triggers adrenaline, breathing speeds up and blood carbon dioxide falls; tingling, dizziness and breathlessness follow, which increase the fear
Quem cruza 2 ou mais fusos: o relógio do: Those crossing 2 or more time zones: the brain's clock adjusts slowly to the new light; until then, sleep and wake hormones, temperature and digestion follow home time (See M2V8 - III)
Tripulação de voos noturnos: entre 2 e 6: Night-flight crews: between 2 and 6 am melatonin is high and body temperature at its lowest; the brain is programmed to sleep, and attention drops (See M2V8 - V)
Quem começou a jornada já cansado: a ade: Those who started the duty already tired: adenosine, which builds up while awake, is only cleared by sleep; those who slept little start in debt and reach the limit sooner (See M2V8 - V)
Tripulação de revezamento: dorme fora do: Relief crews: they sleep outside their biological schedule, in an environment that interrupts sleep, and lose deep and REM sleep, the stages that restore the brain (See M2V8 - VI)
Quem dorme alto sem aclimatação: o oxigê: Those sleeping high without acclimatisation: low oxygen makes you breathe more, carbon dioxide falls, and breathing stops and restarts in cycles, fragmenting sleep (See M2V1)
Quem usa insulina ou remédio que baixa o: Those on insulin or sugar-lowering medicine: the brain depends on glucose and cannot store it; these medicines can lower sugar more than needed, and the signs are confused with those of hypoxia
Quem usa bomba, sobretudo com doses pequ: Pump users, especially on small doses: the reservoir bubble grows on the climb and pushes extra insulin; those on little insulin feel the difference proportionally more
Diabetes descontrolado: o açúcar acima d: Uncontrolled diabetes: sugar above what the kidney can hold back spills into the urine and pulls water with it; together with dry air, this dehydrates
Obesidade (IMC 30 ou mais): o abdome pes: Obesity (BMI 30 or more): the abdomen presses on the pelvic veins, blood returns more slowly from the legs, and excess fat makes the blood more inflamed and prone to clot
Quem usa insulina ou hormônio da tireoid: Those on insulin or thyroid hormone: insulin acts for hours and must match food intake; levothyroxine needs an empty stomach to be well absorbed, and meals at odd times interfere
Não sentem rotação lenta nem curva longa: Do not sense slow rotation or a long turn: they only respond to rotation above a threshold, and in a sustained turn the fluid catches up with the canal and the cupula returns to centre
Confundem aceleração com nariz alto: os: Mistake acceleration for nose-up: the crystals press on the sensory cells and sense gravity and acceleration added together, without telling them apart
Falso horizonte, autocinese, ilusões de: False horizon, autokinesis, runway illusions: without a reliable reference, the brain fills in the scene with what it expects; a fixed light in the dark seems to move because the eye drifts with nothing around it
Desorientação e perda de controle: quand: Disorientation and loss of control: when the eyes, inner ear and body disagree, the brain tends to follow the strongest sensation, which may be wrong
Cinetose: náusea, vômito, sono pelo remé: Motion sickness: nausea, vomiting, drowsiness from medication; the conflict between what the inner ear senses and what the eyes see activates the vomiting centres, and antihistamines cause sedation
A placa estreita a artéria e deixa pouca: Plaque narrows the artery and leaves little margin: with a faster heart, the muscle demands more blood than the narrowed artery can deliver
A troca súbita de ritmo traz palpitação,: A sudden change of rhythm brings palpitations, dizziness and clots: in an irregular rhythm the heart pumps less blood, and in an atrium that does not contract the blood stalls and clots
Infarto, AVC e arritmia podem incapacita: Heart attack, stroke and arrhythmia can incapacitate at once: the brain depends on continuous flow, and an arrhythmia or a clot reaching it cuts off blood within seconds
Insuficiência cardíaca e embolia trazem: Heart failure and embolism bring shortness of breath in the cabin: in heart failure fluid builds up in the lung and in embolism part of it loses its blood supply; with less oxygen in the air, the already reduced exchange is not enough
O sangue parado forma coágulos nos voos: Pooled blood forms clots on long flights: sitting still, the calf does not pump blood back, and slow blood clots more easily
O ar que sobra no peito cresce com a sub: Air left in the chest expands during the climb: trapped in the chest, the gas expands with lower pressure and compresses the lung and the heart
G-LOC entre 4,5 e 6,3 G; cerca de 28 seg: G-LOC between 4.5 and 6.3 G; about 28 seconds without control; jerks and confusion on recovery; blood cannot rise to the brain, which shuts down without oxygen
Perda periférica, acinzentamento e apaga: Peripheral loss, grayout and blackout before G-LOC; red vision with −Gz; pressure inside the eye opposes blood pressure, and the retina loses flow before the brain
Queda de cerca de 22 mmHg por G no nível: Drop of about 22 mmHg per G at eye level; the reflex takes 6 to 9 s; the column of blood between heart and head becomes heavier, and the reflex that speeds the heart and tightens the vessels is slow to respond
Chance cerca de 3 vezes maior de dor no: About 3 times higher chance of neck pain with the highest G; worse when looking back; the neck carries the head and helmet multiplied by G, and when turned it is in a weaker position
A manobra anti-G cansa e pode causar les: The anti-G maneuver is tiring and can cause injury if done at full strength at 1 G; maximally tensing the legs and abdomen and straining against a closed glottis uses a lot of energy and overloads the muscles and chest
Oxygen pressure falls: 108 mmHg at 8,000 ft and 70 mmHg at 18,000 ft; hypoxia begins; with less pressure, less oxygen passes from the lung into the blood, and the brain is the first to feel it
O gás preso cresce 1,4 vez a 8.000 ft e: Trapped gas grows 1.4 times at 8,000 ft and 3 times at 25,000 ft; barotrauma, most often in the middle ear; outside pressure falls and the trapped gas expands (Boyle's law), and the middle ear can only vent through the narrow tube
O nitrogênio dissolvido forma bolhas: do: Dissolved nitrogen forms bubbles: decompression sickness; with lower pressure, blood and tissues hold less dissolved gas (Henry's law)
Ressecamento com a umidade de 10% a 20%: Dryness with humidity of 10% to 20% in cruise; outside air, very cold, holds almost no water vapour, and the mucous membranes lose water to it
Na linha de Armstrong, a 63.000 ft, os l: At the Armstrong line, at 63,000 ft, exposed liquids can boil: ambient pressure falls below the vapour pressure of water at body temperature
Na cabine a 8.000 ft, a saturação cai ce: With the cabin at 8,000 ft, saturation falls about 4 points; above 10,000 ft, hypoxia grows; at night, vision worsens first; with lower oxygen pressure, less oxygen reaches the blood, and the retina and brain, the biggest consumers, feel it first
Mudanças de pressão na subida e na desci: Pressure changes during climb and descent: air in the middle ear and sinuses must leave and enter through narrow openings, and a fast change leaves no time
Respirar sob pressão positiva por muito: Breathing under positive pressure for a long time causes stagnant hypoxia: high pressure in the chest hinders blood return to the heart, and flow to the tissues falls
O ar da cabine é seco e resseca as mucos: Cabin air is dry and dries out the mucous membranes: it comes from outside, where the cold air holds very little water vapour
Perto da linha de Armstrong, a respiraçã: Near the Armstrong line, breathing is no longer enough: even with pure oxygen, the pressure is so low that it cannot push enough oxygen into the blood
Perda temporária e, com os anos, perda p: Temporary loss and, over the years, permanent loss starting near 4,000 Hz; at 140 dB, eardrum rupture; excess sound energy first fatigues and then destroys the hair cells, which do not regenerate
Acima de 90 dB pioram vigilância, concen: Above 90 dB, vigilance, concentration, calculation and sense of time worsen; stress; noise competes for attention and activates the body's alarm response
Possível aumento da pressão arterial; os: Possible rise in blood pressure; the data do not yet allow limits to be set; the proposed mechanism is activation of the alert system, which constricts the vessels
Vibração de 12,5 a 31,5 Hz embaça a visã: Vibration from 12.5 to 31.5 Hz blurs vision and instrument reading: in this range the eye shakes inside the orbit and the image slips on the retina
Dor lombar frequente em pilotos de helic: Frequent low back pain in helicopter pilots; body resonance from 4 to 8 Hz: in this range the spine vibrates more than the seat, and discs and muscles absorb the repeated load
Os tecidos de maior peso no risco de cân: The tissues with the greatest weight in cancer risk: each mSv adds 12 cases in 100,000; these are tissues with rapidly dividing cells, more sensitive to DNA damage
Em comissárias, mais câncer de mama (1,5: In flight attendants, more breast cancer (1.5 times), melanoma (2.3) and non-melanoma skin cancer (4.1); radiation does not explain everything: radiation damages DNA, but sunlight through the windscreen and other factors also play a part
Defeito genético grave: 1,2 por milhão p: Serious genetic defect: 1.2 per million per mSv; radiation can alter the DNA of the cells that form eggs and sperm
Nas três primeiras semanas, pode haver p: In the first three weeks, the embryo may be lost; afterward, fatal cancer 1 in 10,000 per mSv; the embryo and fetus have rapidly dividing cells, more sensitive to DNA damage
Catarata acima de cerca de 0,5 Gy, dose: Cataract above about 0.5 Gy, a dose far above that of flight; damaged lens cells are not replaced and make the lens cloudy
Concentração, memória e decisão mais len: Slower concentration, memory and decisions: depression, anxiety and fatigue drain the energy and attention the brain devotes to the task
Insônia piora o humor; remédio para dorm: Insomnia worsens mood; sleeping pills weigh on the next day: sleep regulates emotions, and the sedative keeps acting on the brain after waking
Álcool e drogas: julgamento, reflexos, d: Alcohol and drugs: judgement, reflexes, dependence; they depress or alter neurons, the liver takes hours to clear them, and repeated use changes the brain's reward circuit
Ansiedade e medo de voar podem virar hip: Anxiety and fear of flying can turn into hyperventilation: adrenaline speeds up breathing, blood carbon dioxide falls, and tingling and dizziness follow
Agitação e impulsividade a bordo: cabine: Agitation and impulsiveness on board: a closed cabin, short sleep and mistimed medicine destabilise those who already have mental illness
A partir de 37,5 °C caem atenção, visão: From 37.5 °C attention, vision and decision-making decline; above 40.6 °C, heatstroke with confusion and coma; neurons work poorly above the normal temperature range, and extreme heat damages cells
Sede só com 2% do peso perdido; 5%, fadi: Thirst only at 2% of body weight lost; 5%, fatigue and nausea; then confusion and kidney failure; with less water, blood volume falls, and the brain and kidney receive less flow
Por volta de 34 °C, o cérebro fica mais: At around 34 °C, the brain slows down: the chemical reactions of neurons slow down in the cold
Abaixo de 30 °C, coração lento e risco d: Below 30 °C, slow heart and risk of arrhythmia; afterdrop can trigger it; cold heart muscle conducts the impulse poorly, and cold blood returning from the limbs cools the heart even further
No primeiro minuto, o choque frio faz of: In the first minute, cold shock causes gasping and inhaling water: sudden cold on the skin triggers a reflex gasp and rapid breathing
Cerca de 10 minutos de movimentos úteis: About 10 minutes of useful movement before they fail: the cold chills the muscles and nerves of the arms and legs, which lose strength and coordination
Fratura por compressão em 20% a 30% das: Compression fracture in 20% to 30% of ejections; 61.6% of serious injuries; grounds the pilot for 3 to 4 months; upward acceleration drives the trunk into the seat along the axis of the vertebrae, which collapse under compression
Trauma craniano; sem capacete, risco 6,3: Head trauma; without a helmet, 6.3 times higher risk of fatal head injury; the head strikes the structure or is jolted, and the brain hits the inside of the skull
Fraturas cervicais na ejeção; carga extr: Cervical fractures in ejection; extra load from the weight of the helmet; the neck carries the head and helmet multiplied by the acceleration
27,3% das lesões graves na ejeção; fratu: 27.3% of serious injuries in ejection; femur fracture on impact; loose arms and legs strike the cockpit or are flailed by the wind, and the femur takes the impact load through the knees
Cinto fora do lugar desloca a carga para: A belt out of place shifts the load to the belly: above the pelvic bones, the belt presses on organs and vessels with no bony protection
Na descompressão explosiva, o ar preso n: In explosive decompression, air trapped in the chest can injure the lung: outside pressure falls faster than the air can escape, and the alveoli overstretch until they rupture
Hipóxia quase imediata; acima de 43.000: Almost immediate hypoxia; above 43,000 ft, 9 to 12 useful seconds; in decompression sickness, confusion, seizures and loss of consciousness; with very low pressure oxygen even moves from the blood back into the lung, and bubbles can block vessels in the brain
Dor profunda nas grandes articulações, a: Deep pain in the large joints, the most common form of decompression sickness: nitrogen bubbles form in the tissues around the joint and press on the nerve endings
Dormência, ardor e formigamento: bolhas: Numbness, burning and tingling: bubbles compress the nerves or cut off the blood that feeds them
Dor em queimação, tosse seca e falta de: Burning pain, dry cough and shortness of breath; can kill without treatment; many bubbles reach the lung through the veins and clog the pulmonary circulation
Coceira e pele marmorizada: bolhas nos p: Itching and mottled skin: bubbles in the small vessels and the tissue under the skin
Voar a 8.000 ft após mergulhar equivale: Flying at 8,000 ft after diving is equivalent to climbing to 40,000 ft without pressurization: the extra nitrogen absorbed while diving forms bubbles at the lower cabin pressure
Raciocínio lento com pouco oxigênio; con: Slow thinking with little oxygen; seizures, fainting, stroke; the brain uses a lot of oxygen and glucose with no stores, and any drop in flow shows quickly
Ar preso depois de cirurgia ou trauma se: Air trapped after surgery or injury expands during the climb, and the rigid skull leaves no room: the air compresses the brain
AVC e AIT: novo evento longe do hospital: Stroke and TIA: a new event far from a hospital; soon after the first event the risk of another is higher, and treatment depends on arriving in time
Aura da enxaqueca tira parte da visão: u: Migraine aura takes away part of the vision: a wave of electrical activity spreads across the visual cortex
Fraqueza, rigidez, quedas: nas doenças d: Weakness, stiffness, falls: in movement disorders the circuits that control the muscles work poorly, and cabin motion worsens balance
Dor, surdez, zumbido e perfuração na des: Pain, deafness, tinnitus and perforation on descent: with the tube closed the middle-ear air is not replenished, and outside pressure pushes the eardrum inward
Vertigem alternobárica e fístula; vertig: Alternobaric vertigo and fistula; incapacitating vertigo: different pressure in the two ears stimulates one labyrinth more than the other, and a fistula lets pressure reach the inner ear
Ruído mascara a fala e lesa o ouvido com: Noise masks speech and damages the ear over time: excess sound energy destroys hair cells, which do not regenerate
Aerossinusite com dor forte na descida:: Aerosinusitis with severe pain on descent: with the sinus opening closed, the vacuum pulls on the lining, which swells and may bleed
Barodontalgia em dente doente ou recém-t: Barodontalgia in a diseased or recently treated tooth: gas trapped in the tooth or an inflamed pulp senses the pressure change
Açúcar baixo: confusão, desmaio, incapac: Low sugar: confusion, fainting, sudden incapacitation; the brain depends on blood glucose and cannot store it
Tireoide acelerada: taquicardia; obesida: Overactive thyroid: tachycardia; obesity: thrombosis; excess hormone speeds up the heart, and the weight presses on the veins and makes the blood more prone to clot
Hipoventilação e apneia: oxigênio baixo: Hypoventilation and apnoea: low oxygen in flight; the weight of the chest and abdomen reduces breathing, and the cabin takes away even more oxygen
Açúcar alto e SGLT2: mais urina e desidr: High sugar and SGLT2 inhibitors: more urine and dehydration; sugar lost in the urine pulls water with it
Doença de Graves: visão dupla; açúcar al: Graves' disease: double vision; high sugar: blurred vision; in Graves' disease the eye muscles swell, and high sugar changes the water content of the lens and the focus
Adaptação ao escuro piora com hipóxia e: Dark adaptation worsens with hypoxia and strong light: rods use a lot of oxygen, and bright light bleaches the pigment they take minutes to rebuild
Olho seco, irritação, lesão por lente de: Dry eye, irritation, contact lens injury: dry air evaporates tears, and the dried-out lens covers a cornea that receives less oxygen
Miopia de campo vazio, presbiopia, borrã: Empty-field myopia, presbyopia, blur from vibration: with nothing to focus on the eye relaxes to near focus, the lens stiffens with age, and vibration moves the image off its place on the retina
Confusão entre vermelho, branco e verde:: Confusion between red, white and green: one of the cone types that separate colours is missing or works poorly
Glaucoma e doenças tiram partes do campo: Glaucoma and diseases take away parts of the field: high pressure or disease damages the optic nerve fibres, which do not recover
Gás que expande, halos e ofuscamento: o: Expanding gas, halos and glare: the injected gas grows during the climb, and the operated cornea scatters light
Reação lenta, lapsos e microssonos depoi: Slow reactions, lapses and microsleeps after 16 to 20 h awake or with accumulated sleep loss; adenosine builds up in the brain while awake, and only sleep clears it
Descompasso com o horário local por dias: Out of step with local time for days after crossing time zones: the brain's clock adjusts slowly to the light of the new place
Melatonina e cortisol fora de hora; meno: Melatonin and cortisol at the wrong time; less growth hormone without sleep: they follow the body clock and deep sleep, which time zones and duty hours displace
Mais grelina, menos leptina e pior uso d: More ghrelin, less leptin and poorer glucose use with short nights: without sleep, the hunger hormone rises, the satiety hormone falls and cells respond less to insulin
Mal-estar e alteração do intestino no je: Malaise and bowel changes with jet lag: the gut has its own clock and keeps home time
Irritação e queda do humor com o sono cu: Irritability and low mood with short sleep and a disrupted clock, because sleep regulates emotions
Apneia e respiração periódica em altitud: Apnea and periodic breathing at altitude fragment sleep: each pause lowers oxygen and makes the brain wake up to breathe
Julgamento, atenção e coordenação falham: Judgment, attention and coordination fail before the person notices; then memory, reasoning and fine movements; the brain uses a lot of oxygen and has no stores, and the most complex functions fail first
A visão noturna piora já em altitudes mo: Night vision worsens even at moderate altitudes: the retina's rods use a lot of oxygen
Anemia e monóxido de carbono reduzem o o: Anemia and carbon monoxide reduce the oxygen carried: with less haemoglobin, or with it taken up by carbon monoxide, the blood carries less oxygen
Fluxo insuficiente, como nas acelerações: Insufficient flow, as in accelerations, causes stagnant hypoxia: the blood has oxygen but does not reach the tissue
A hiperventilação baixa o gás carbônico: Hyperventilation lowers carbon dioxide and causes tingling and spasms: the blood becomes alkaline, less free calcium remains, and nerves and muscles become irritable
Ar preso no pneumotórax e nas bolhas cre: Air trapped in a pneumothorax or in bullae grows about 38% at 8,000 ft: with no way out, the gas expands at lower pressure and compresses the lung
Crise de asma ou piora da DPOC longe do: Asthma attack or COPD worsening far from medical care: the diseased lung has less reserve for the low cabin oxygen, and dry air irritates the airways
A apneia sem tratamento traz sonolência: Untreated apnea brings sleepiness and errors: the pauses fragment sleep and lower oxygen at night
Lábios azulados podem aparecer, mas sua: Bluish lips may appear, but their absence does not rule out hypoxia: the colour depends on the amount of haemoglobin without oxygen and on the light, and changes little at first
Por que o intestino incha dentro de um a: Why does the intestine become bloated inside an aircraft?
A azia e a úlcera impedem de voar?: Do heartburn and ulcers prevent flying?
Diarreia, intestino irritável e doença i: Diarrhea, irritable bowel syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease
Quando uma crise intestinal torna o voo: When does an intestinal flare-up make flying unsafe?
Hepatites, gordura no fígado e cirrose: Hepatitis, fatty liver disease and cirrhosis
O que o fígado doente muda na segurança: How does liver disease affect flight safety?
Um cálculo sem dor tem o mesmo risco que: Does a painless gallstone carry the same risk as an acute attack?
Quanto esperar para voar depois de uma c: How long should you wait to fly after surgery?
Por que o intestino pode distender na su: Why can the intestines become distended during ascent?
O ar ocupa mais volume com a queda da pr: Air takes up more volume as pressure falls
O gás ocupa mais volume quando a pressão: Gas takes up more volume when pressure decreases.
Quem sofre mais risco com gás que expand: Who is at greater risk from expanding gas?
Pessoa com obstrução intestinal ou sutur: A person with bowel obstruction or a recent suture
Gás retido ou suturas recentes aumentam: Trapped gas or recent sutures increase the risk of pain and injury.
Vômito com sangue ou fezes negras com ma: Vomiting blood or black stools accompanied by feeling unwell
Esses sintomas exigem avaliação urgente: These symptoms require urgent assessment before a flight.
Qual conduta cabe ao tripulante com úlce: What should a crew member with an active ulcer and significant pain do?
Continuar se usar antiácido: Continue working while taking an antacid
Afastar-se e fazer avaliação aeromédica: Stop flying and obtain an aeromedical assessment
A dor pode incapacitar e os remédios não: Pain may cause incapacitation, and medication does not prove that an ulcer has healed.
Quando a loperamida não deve ser usada i: When should loperamide not be used on its own?
Com febre ou sangue nas fezes: When there is fever or blood in the stool
No começo de viagem longa: At the start of a long journey
Febre ou sangue sugerem doença que preci: Fever or blood may indicate a condition that needs medical assessment.
Qual situação permite considerar aptidão: Under European Class 1 guidance, when may fitness be considered in inflammatory bowel disease?
Doença em remissão estável sem corticoid: Stable remission without systemic corticosteroids for disease control
A remissão clínica e a estabilidade do t: Clinical remission and stable treatment are key conditions.
O fígado deixa de depurar substâncias qu: The liver fails to clear substances that affect the brain
Encefalopatia hepática pode provocar con: Hepatic encephalopathy can cause confusion and incapacitation.
Qual sinal de doença biliar impede embar: Which sign of biliary disease calls for assessment before boarding?
Febre, dor forte e icterícia com mal-est: Fever, severe pain and jaundice with feeling unwell
Esses sintomas podem indicar inflamação: These symptoms may indicate active inflammation or obstruction.
O passageiro deve evitar voo durante qua: According to the UK CAA, how long should passengers avoid flying after abdominal surgery?
A recomendação aos passageiros é evitar: Passenger guidance recommends avoiding the first 10 days; recovery may require longer.
Qual é o prazo indicado ao passageiro ap: What is the suggested waiting period for a passenger after an uncomplicated colonoscopy with substantial gas insufflation?
A referência para passageiros recomenda: The passenger reference recommends 24 hours; the procedure and clinical recovery also need consideration.
Qual é a orientação britânica para o pil: What does UK guidance advise for pilots after lower gastrointestinal endoscopy with biopsy or polypectomy?
Pelo menos 48 horas e avisar o examinado: Wait at least 48 hours and inform the medical examiner
Para o piloto, a orientação é de pelo me: For pilots, the advice is to wait at least 48 hours and inform the AME.
24 horas dizem respeito apenas ao gás re: 24 hours only concerns residual gas in the abdomen, not healing from major surgery.

A **diarreia** elimina água e sais pelas:
**Diarrhea** causes the loss of water and salts through the stool; it can be caused by infection, medication or inflammation. **Irritable bowel syndrome** causes pain and changes in bowel habits without the destructive inflammation characteristic of **Crohn's disease** and **ulcerative colitis**.

In the cabin, urgency to evacuate and limited access to the bathroom can compromise tasks. **Intense diarrhea** causes dehydration: less blood volume causes weakness, dizziness and a drop in blood pressure. **Blood in the stool**, fever and severe pain suggest a complication that should not be treated as mere travel discomfort.

**Passenger** with mild, tolerable symptoms and without fever or significant dehydration can travel if they are able to keep fluids; a serious crisis requires assessment before embarking. For the **crew member**, stable inflammatory disease may be compatible with fitness after evaluation: the FAA provides criteria for colitis and the European standard requires stable remission in the 1st class, without systemic corticosteroids for control.

An exacerbation with pain, bleeding or disabling diarrhea can suddenly remove the crew member from duty. At the FAA, following a special authorization for colitis requires reevaluation when the disease worsens, requires surgery or requires certain medications; operating during an exacerbation is contrary to the fitness requirement.

**Oral rehydration solution** replaces water and electrolytes in significant losses. **Loperamide** can relieve non-bloody diarrhea, but should not be used alone if there is **fever or blood in the stool**. Antibiotics are not routine prevention; treatment of infections, corticosteroids and immunosuppressants requires a medical plan. For crew members, the effects and underlying illness need assessment.

**How ​​to prevent and alleviate it.** Before traveling, have safe water, tolerated food and prescribed medicines in your carry-on luggage. Replace losses and avoid boarding with dehydration, fever, blood in the stool or incapacitating crisis. The crew member must leave during exacerbations and return after evaluating clinical control and treatment.
A **vesícula biliar** guarda a bile prod:
The **gallbladder** stores the bile produced by the liver. **Gallstones** can remain silent or block the flow of bile, producing colic, inflammation and jaundice. The **pancreas** releases digestive enzymes; when it becomes inflamed, **pancreatitis** can cause intense pain, vomiting and systemic illness.

An attack of biliary colic or pancreatitis is not just a stomach ache. **Obstruction**, inflammation and vomiting can progress without adequate assistance during the flight. Expansion of gas in the intestine can add distension, but is not the cause of stones or pancreatitis.

**Passengers** with asymptomatic stones and no complications can receive medical advice to travel; persistent pain, fever, jaundice with malaise and significant vomiting require prior evaluation. **Crew** requires individual aeromedical decision: in European standards, symptomatic stones and active pancreatitis prevent fitness; asymptomatic stone can be considered after assessment according to class and context.

A sudden crisis may disable you from commanding or serving in the cabin. The FAA has separate provisions for stones and pancreatitis; ANAC assesses the risk of digestive incapacitation. Returning after pain has improved without clarifying the cause is not enough to confirm fitness.

Analgesics and antispasmodics can hide the worsening or cause drowsiness; after gallbladder surgery, the abdominal procedure recovery criteria also apply. **Antibiotics**, surgery or other treatments should be guided by the cause, not an improvised pre-flight dose.

**How ​​to prevent and alleviate it.** Differentiate the presence of stones without symptoms from a recent episode of obstruction, fever, severe pain or pancreatitis. Take the report and therapeutic plan, avoid foods that trigger pain individually and don't embark on a crisis. The crew member returns only when the cause is controlled, without disabling effects and after aeromedical evaluation.
